claims.claim: Samuel Butler's prose translation, Ulysses and Minerva names
claims.evidence: 'Butler's Translation of the Odyssey appeared originally in 1900'; Ulysses, Minerva throughout

claims.claim: Book I opens with invocation to the Muse
claims.evidence: 'Tell me, O Muse, of that ingenious hero'

claims.claim: Gods pity Ulysses, held by Calypso
claims.evidence: 'all the gods had pity on him save Poseidon' / 'now begun to pity him except Neptune'; Calypso on the Ogygian island

claims.claim: Minerva goes to Ithaca to urge Telemachus to seek news while suitors waste the house
claims.evidence: book I heading 'MINERVA'S VISIT TO ITHACA'; 'I will also conduct him to Sparta and to Pylos'
'Ulysses, who ruled them as though he were their father'

claims.claim: Held for years on Calypso's island, Ogygia
claims.evidence: text names it 'the Ogygian' island ('Ogygia' not written)
claims.fix: Held for years on Calypso's island, the Ogygian island

claims.claim: The gods free him; he reaches the Phaeacians, who send him home
claims.evidence: Mercury sent to Calypso (l.395); 'RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS'; 'conveyed' home

claims.claim: He tells of the Cyclops, Circe, the Sirens and his lost men
claims.evidence: 'savage Cyclops'; 'Circe'; 'First you will come to the Sirens'; 'could not save his men'

claims.claim: Penelope holds off suitors; Telemachus goes seeking news
Home in disguise, Ulysses meets the swineherd Eumaeus and his son
claims.evidence: 'ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS'; Telemachus meets him there

claims.claim: Strings the great bow, kills the suitors with Telemachus
claims.evidence: 'whomsoever of you shall string it'; Minerva 'doomed him to fall by the hand of Telemachus'
book XXIII; Butler note 'why could she not at once ask to see the scar'

claims.claim: Minerva makes peace with the dead suitors' kin
claims.evidence: 'presently made a covenant of peace between the'

claims.claim: Characters: Ulysses, Penelope, Telemachus, Minerva, Eumaeus, Calypso, Alcinous
